items.title: Tribunal says India cannot withdraw from water treaty with Pakistan
items.summary: THE HAGUE: An international tribunal on Monday ordered India to "observe its obligations" under a treaty with Pakistan on the sharing of the Indus and other rivers, which the New Delhi government sought to suspend. It also made an order "prohibiting" India from carrying out works at two hydro-electric projects that could breach the 1960 Indus Water Treaty. India's Water Minister C.R.

items.title: Three killed, one injured after car plunges into five-metre-deep ravine
items.summary: Lahad Datu Fire and Rescue Station chief Sumsoa Rashid said the department received an emergency call at 7.38pm. He said firefighters who arrived at the scene found four men involved in the accident. "Three victims were confirmed dead by Health Ministry personnel at the scene.

items.title: Two killed, four injured in Mersing boat collision
items.summary: MERSING: Two people were killed while four others were injured after two boats collided near Kuala Sungai Mersing tonight. The Fire and Rescue Department operations centre spokesman, quoted by Bernama, said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 9.04pm. Following the call, a team of nine men from the Mersing Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to Mersing jetty.

items.title: Iran says 10 missing fishermen found in UAE
items.summary: TEHERAN: Ten Iranian fishermen who went missing in Gulf waters weeks ago are alive in the United Arab Emirates and set to travel home soon, Iran's foreign ministry said on Monday. Mohammad Soleimani, head of the ministry's representative office in Hormozgan province, said 13 fishermen had been missing since early August, amid concerns they may have been arrested after entering the territorial waters of neighbouring countries. Iranian media have also reported another case involving fishermen missing since May.

items.title: Man suffers burns as fire spreads to nine factory lots in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH: A man suffered burns to his body after a fire spread to nine factory lots in Persiaran Industri Bercham 10, Bercham, here this afternoon. Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the 42-year-old man suffered burns to one per cent of his body in the incident and received first aid from emergency medical rescue services personnel at the scene. "Other affected factories included Lots 10 and 11, which suffered 20 per cent damage; Lots 12, 13 and 14 (70 per cent); Lots 16 and 18 (80 per cent); Lot 15 (10 per cent); and Lot 17 (60 per cent)," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Iran war spurs Gulf investment in infrastructure
items.summary: Gulf governments are looking at ways to create permanent, integrated solutions to get round using Hormuz, said an industry source. Ports have emerged as a "mission-critical priority" for Gulf governments, including Saudi Arabia, said a second industry source. "If two years ago sports was the big buzz thing, I think for the time being, next year or two, they're going to say ports, ports, ports," he said of Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Vietnam coffee farmers ride China's durian wave
items.summary: VIETNAM'S Central Highlands produces around one sixth of the world's coffee, but farmers are switching their traditional crop for durian to cash in on surging Chinese demand for the pungent "king of fruits". "You can live okay with coffee, but it's durian that makes you rich," said Pham Xuan Lan, as he showed AFP journalists around his farm. Vietnam only officially entered the Chinese durian market after a 2022 trade protocol but last year became the country's biggest supplier by volume, ending Thailand's nearly two-decade dominance.

items.title: Haze: Sarikei hits 303, bringing Sarawak's hazardous API areas to five
items.summary: According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Sarikei recorded an API reading of 303. Nine other stations recorded unhealthy readings, including Bintulu (189), ILP Miri (179), Miri (179), Kapit (171) and Limbang (162) in Sarawak. Meanwhile, 45 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality, while Langkawi recorded the country's only "good" API reading at 45.

items.title: Iraq sentences kidnapper of US journalist to 15 years in prison
items.summary: BAGHDAD: Iraq's judiciary has sentenced a man to 15 years in prison for the kidnapping of an American journalist who was abducted earlier this year by a powerful Iran-backed group, a judicial source said Monday. A judicial source verified the document's authenticity to AFP, and a Kataeb Hezbollah source confirmed the ruling against one of its members. The issue has fuelled tensions in Iraq, with several groups, including Kataeb Hezbollah, refusing to disarm.

items.title: NST Leader: Subsidies are a lifeline, not a bottomless well
items.summary: TODAY, the reinstatement of the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) subsidy quota of 300 litres per Malaysian kicks in, a reprieve for citizens burdened by inflation. Although the United States-Iran war is driving up oil prices, the government made a difficult decision: rather than deprive Malaysians of fuel subsidies, it will help absorb the costly expenditure. Malaysians must not view the quota reinstatement as a sign that the government's financial position has become stronger.

items.title: Pakistan says welcomes Hague decision on water-sharing treaty with India
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan welcomed on Monday a decision by an international tribunal that a landmark water-sharing treaty remained in force, despite India's suspension of its participation. "Pakistan welcomes this finding by the Court that interim measures are warranted," the government said in a statement following the decision by the Court of Arbitration in The Hague requiring India to pause work on a dam project. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Nine secondary school students hurt in Sabah tour bus accident
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Nine secondary school students sustained minor injuries after the tour bus they were travelling in was involved in an accident at the Jalan Kota Belud-Kundasang T-junction today. Kota Belud Fire and Rescue Station chief Elge Bakuk said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 11am. He said the tour bus had been chartered to transport 35 students and a teacher from the school.

items.title: At least 2,500 buildings destroyed in Nepal valley
items.summary: PARIS: More than 2,500 buildings were destroyed in Nepal's Trishuli valley in tsunami-like glacial floods on August 26, according to an AFP computation of data from Europe's Copernicus observatory. That's about two-thirds of all buildings in the three potentially affected zones studied by Copernicus' Emergency Management Service. Ten kilometres further south, the disaster-stricken area of Syabrubesi lost nearly three-quarters of its buildings.

items.title: Lorry driver arrested with RM200k worth of ornamental plant saplings
items.summary: RANTAU PANJANG: A lorry driver was arrested after 6,000 ornamental plant saplings worth RM200,000, believed to have been smuggled from Thailand, were seized at Kampung Padang Licin here today. General Operations Force Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the seized plants comprised 2,000 frangipani, 2,000 cermai and 2,000 cactus plants. "A 61-year-old man who was driving the lorry was later arrested," he said.

items.title: Indonesia battles surge in forest fires as West Kalimantan hotspots nearly double
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia is battling a sharp surge in forest and land fires in parts of Kalimantan, with hotspots in West Kalimantan nearly doubling to 7,377 on Monday. "In Central Kalimantan, hotspots declined by 147 to 5,244, but fire spots increased by 16 to 72, while in South Kalimantan, hotspots fell by 405 to 504, but fire spots rose by 33 to 55," he told an online press conference on Monday. The number of fire spots also decreased across the three provinces.

items.title: Indonesia raises 2027 subsidised fuel allocation, keeps LPG unchanged
items.summary: Here are the details: • Indonesia will allocate 19 million kilolitres of subsidised diesel in 2027, about 2 per cent higher than this year's allocation of 18.64 million kilolitres. • Energy ministry senior official Laode Sulaeman said at a separate meeting that subsidised diesel consumption this year is expected to reach 20.27 million kilolitres, exceeding the original allocation. • The subsidised LPG allocation for next year is set at 8 million metric tons, unchanged from this year, but lower than the 8.67 million tons expected to be consumed this year.

items.title: No automatic invitations to ex-PMs for National Day celebrations since 2018, says secretariat
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Former prime ministers have not been automatically invited to the National Day celebrations since 2018, the National Day 2026 secretariat said today. Secretariat chairman Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah said invitations for major official federal government events were managed by the Prime Minister's Department's Protocol and International Conference Secretariat Division. "Based on the practice since 2018, invitations to the National Day celebrations are not automatically extended to former prime ministers.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - August 31, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Here are today's top stories. Fuel quotas Improved supply management, stricter enforcement and the government's sound fiscal position were key factors in the restoration of Budi Madani fuel quotas from 200 to 300 litres. Hazardous Sarawak's air quality continued to worsen , with four monitoring stations recording hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today.

items.title: Anwar's 6 initiatives proof government listens to people, says Nga
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The six key initiatives announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in his 2026 National Day Address yesterday take into account public feedback and the people's daily needs, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said. He said the six initiatives would directly benefit the people, covering fuel subsidies, school maintenance, healthcare facilities, artificial intelligence (AI) training, e-Invoicing, as well as assistance for small traders and small and medium enterprises. "The six initiatives announced by the Prime Minister are concrete proof that the Madani government listens to the pulse of the people and consistently prioritises their well-being.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Monday, Aug 31, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1522950]] [[nid:1522947]] [[nid:1522944]] [[nid:1522943]] [[nid:1522942]] [[nid:1522941]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: 18-year-old college student dies after falling from 22nd-floor condominium
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An 18-year-old private college student died after he fell from the 22nd floor of a residential premises in Setapak here this morning. Wangsa Maju district police chief Assistant Commissioner Annas Sulaiman said the victim, a first-semester student at the college, was seen arriving at the premises at 7.07am. He said the condominium had been converted into a hostel for students of the private college.

items.title: For young PJ councillor, nation-building starts in his own 'kampung'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "I just want to make my corner of the country a little better," said Loh Y Lun, who hopes to be remembered simply as a Malaysian who rolled up his sleeves and served his community. Taking up the role, Loh hopes to address everyday problems and improve services for residents. Loh said the role was especially fulfilling because he was serving the city that shaped him.

items.title: Printed books remain a favourite despite rise of digital reading
items.summary: Despite the widespread availability of digital platforms, many readers maintain that physical books have a timeless appeal that electronic screens simply cannot replicate. "With physical books, there is a real sense of satisfaction. "Physical books are crucial, especially colourful ones.

items.title: Sri Lanka's ex-finance minister arrested over alleged corruption
items.summary: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka's former finance minister Ravi Karunanayake was arrested on Monday for allegedly using state funds to pay his private employees, the country's main anti-corruption body said. The former cabinet minister was taken into custody by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) following a lengthy interrogation. The arrest of Karunanayake, a member of former president Ranil Wickremesinghe's administration, comes amid a widespread crackdown on corruption by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, who took office in 2024.

items.title: Budi Madani: Restored RON95 quota, higher diesel allocation bring relief to motorists, traders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The government’s decision to restore the assistance quota under the Budi Madani programme for RON95 petrol and increase the diesel quota has been well received by various layers of society and traders, considering it a timely step in alleviating the burden of living costs. In the address, he announced that the basic eligibility quota for RON95 petrol subsidies would be increased from 200 litres to 300 litres, while the Budi Diesel quota would be raised from 300 litres to 400 litres, effective today. Private sector worker, Furzani Ahmad, 24, said that the return of this quota contributed tremendously towards his commute to work.

items.title: Sarawak sees rise in respiratory infection, conjunctivitis cases amid worsening air quality
items.summary: KUCHING: Sarawak has recorded an increase in upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) and conjunctivitis cases amid deteriorating air quality since early August, with weekly URTI cases rising to 1,752 from about 1,717 at the beginning of the year. "The Southern Zone recorded about 1,250 cases, while the Central Zone recorded more than 1,000 cases and the Northern Zone recorded a peak of almost 400 cases," he said in a statement today. From January to the end of August 2026, the sentinel health facilities recorded about 694,800 patient visits, including 64,688 URTI cases and 6,156 asthma cases.

items.title: Wanted man arrested after high-speed chase, second suspect on the run
items.summary: A second suspect in the same vehicle fled on foot and is being hunted by police. City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the incident occurred about 9.30am when Bukit Aman highway traffic police on patrol spotted a suspicious green four-wheel-drive vehicle near the toll plaza heading towards Klang. He said police arrested the 29-year-old driver, while the second suspect escaped on foot.

items.title: College student dies after fall from Setapak condominium
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — An 18-year-old college student died after falling from the 22nd floor of a condominium in Setapak here this morning. Free Malaysia Today reported that Wangsa Maju police chief Annas Sulaiman said police were alerted at about 8.50am after a security guard found the student’s body at Residensi Teratai on Jalan Langkawi. Annas said the footage showed the student subsequently falling from a corridor on the 22nd floor to the sixth floor.

items.title: Singapore to send humanitarian aid to Nepal for flood relief
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore will send humanitarian supplies and personnel to Nepal to support relief efforts following severe flash floods near the Nepal-China border, the Foreign Ministry said. In a statement, the ministry said Singapore Police Force (SPF) officers specialising in Disaster Victim Identification (DVI) would be deployed at Nepal's request, while civilian and Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) supplies would also be delivered. "In addition, the government will deliver humanitarian assistance comprising both civilian and Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) supplies to Nepal," the ministry said.

items.title: HONOR X9e Pro smartphone makes first appearance at National Day Parade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HONOR has given Malaysians their first public look at the all-new HONOR X9e Pro, with the unreleased smartphone appearing in a striking purple finish at the National Day parade. The event also marked HONOR's first appearance at Malaysia's national-level National Day parade, with the company bringing its humanoid robot to the celebrations. Its consecutive appearances at the two major Malaysian events saw the humanoid robot receive Asia Record and Asean Record certifications for being the "First Humanoid Robot to Complete a 10-Kilometre Public Road Run and March in a National Day Parade".

items.title: Kuala Krai Market echoes with patriotic songs, traders wear Jalur Gemilang attire
items.summary: KUALA KRAI: The atmosphere at Kuala Krai Market was different today when nearly 30 traders donned attire featuring the colours of the Jalur Gemilang, while patriotic songs rang out to enliven the National Day celebrations. Bernama's survey found that the traders were not merely doing business as usual but took the opportunity to foster the spirit of love for the country by turning the market into a location to nurture patriotism among the community. The red, white, blue and yellow colours of the Jalur Gemilang clearly brightened the market space, while the traders' unique appearance also attracted the attention of visitors who came to purchase their daily necessities.

items.title: Mat Sabu: Malaysia needs rice self-sufficiency rate of at least 80pc for secure supply
items.summary: In another development, Mohamad said the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry wants to explore an approach to integrating giant freshwater prawn farming in rice fields to produce two sources of yield from the same agricultural area. He said he saw the potential of this approach during his visit to a rice field area that integrated rice cultivation with giant freshwater prawn farming China two weeks ago. “In that rice field, there are giant freshwater prawns, there are two yields, one from rice and one from prawns….the giant freshwater prawn fry were brought from Malaysia and breeding was carried out in China.

items.title: Malaysia's rice self-sufficiency ratio needs to reach 80 per cent, says Mohamad
items.summary: He said his ministry would continue to strengthen the country's rice ecosystem and increase domestic rice production to ensure sufficient supply, as an SSR of below 60 per cent was inadequate for the country's food security. In another development, Mohamad said his ministry wanted to explore an approach to integrating giant freshwater prawn farming with rice cultivation to produce two sources of yield from the same agricultural area. He said he saw the potential of the approach during a visit to a rice-growing area where rice cultivation was integrated with giant freshwater prawn farming in China two weeks ago.

items.title: Haze worsens in East Malaysia as Sarawak records hazardous API, Sabah unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Haze conditions remained severe in East Malaysia today, with four areas in Sarawak recording hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm, while four areas in Sabah registered unhealthy levels by 6pm. Three other areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy readings, namely Sarikei at 277, Sibu at 243 and Mukah at 216. Meanwhile, Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic and Kimanis in Sabah recorded moderate API readings of 121 and 116 respectively, while 42 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings and three recorded good readings as of 4pm.

items.title: Malaysia seeks Nepal’s nod to deploy SMART team for flood SAR mission, says Tok Mat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Malaysia has sought permission from the Nepalese government to deploy the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations following the floods in the country. “The discussion focused on the latest developments in the SAR operations, particularly efforts to locate Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal recently,” Mohamad wrote on his official Facebook page. On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported as saying that the Madani Government has decided to send the SMART Team to Nepal to assist with SAR operations following the flood disaster that hit the country.

items.title: MAHA 2026 attracts 1.8 million visitors, records RM6m sales in three days
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 31 — The Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 has recorded 1.8 million visitors and nearly RM6 million in sales in its first three days, says Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said 184,000 vehicles were recorded entering and leaving the exhibition grounds during the period, reflecting heavy traffic due to the large turnout. “Three days have passed, and visitor turnout for MAHA has reached 1.8 million, with 184,000 vehicles moving in and out.

items.title: Three-year-old boy injured after foot run over by tow vehicle at Terengganu National Day parade
items.summary: The boy’s mother, Puteri Anis Athirah Wan Rosli, 36, from Cendering, said the incident occurred at about 9.45 am in front of Wisma Persekutuan here. She said her son, Che Ku Muhammad Khairul Amir Che Ku Mohd Khairul Azlan, fell before being run over by the tow vehicle carrying a Fire and Rescue Department boat. My son followed her.

items.title: AI programme to equip 100,000 youths for changing job market, says HR minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The AI for the People Programme, which targets 100,000 youths aged between 18 and 30, is an important step towards preparing Malaysia’s workforce for rapid changes in the employment landscape, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan. He said access to artificial intelligence (AI) technology should be expanded among youth to ensure they possessed skills relevant to the needs of the current job market and were not left behind in global technologicl developments. “As such, providing 100,000 youths with access to AI technology is an important investment to equip Malaysian talent with relevant skills and ensure they are not left behind in the changing global job landscape,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Armizan: Political maturity key to keeping unity govt stable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Political maturity and the awareness of balancing political rights with the responsibility of nation-building are important to ensure the stability of the Unity Government, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. In a Facebook post in conjunction with National Day today, he said the new political landscape of the country after the 15th General Election (GE15) needs to be accepted with the awareness that government stability is crucial in steering the direction of national development and the welfare of the people. He said the country’s new political landscape after the end of one-party dominance must be accepted by taking lessons from the experience between 2018 and 2022 which saw the change of three prime ministers and three Cabinet line-ups in one term.

items.title: King Charles conveys National Day message to Sultan Ibrahim, praises partnership and shared Commonwealth values
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — King Charles III and Queen Camilla have conveyed their congratulations to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the people of Malaysia on the country’s National Day on Monday. In the message shared by the British High Commission in Malaysia, King Charles expressed confidence that the UK-Malaysia Strategic Partnership would provide a valuable opportunity to deepen cooperation between the two countries in trade, technology and other shared priorities ahead of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027. Meanwhile, King Charles also reflected upon the enduring partnership between the two nations, rooted in the shared values and mutual respect that define the Commonwealth.

items.title: Sabah CM Hajiji announces RM3,000 aid for each household hit by Kota Kinabalu fire
items.summary: Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the amount comprised RM1,000 contributions each from the state government, the federal government and the Yayasan Kebajikan Sabah. He said the state government would also assist efforts to rebuild the victims’ homes through coordination between the State Secretary’s Office and Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA). Hajiji said that on humanitarian grounds, each non-Malaysian KIR affected by the fire in the village would also receive RM1,000 in aid from the state government.

items.title: Family prays for Gelugor hiker missing in Nepal floods, Penang government ready to assist
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 31 — The family of Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, who has reportedly remained unreachable following flash floods and landslides in the Nepal-Tibet border area in Nepal last Wednesday, hopes that the hiker will be found safe. He said the family, who live in Taman Tun Sardon, Gelugor, here, were currently in Kuala Lumpur to follow developments concerning Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, who works with the Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM) Penang, through Wisma Putra. “Yesterday, family members attended a meeting with Wisma Putra to obtain information about Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, and until now, we have also not received any phone calls or messages from him in Nepal.

items.title: From midnight to noon, Hospital Tunku Azizah welcomes 12 Merdeka babies including twin girls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — As the nation celebrated its 69th National Day, 12 newborns, including a pair of twin girls, began their life stories at Hospital Tunku Azizah (HTA) here today. All ten ‘Merdeka babies’ were delivered between midnight and noon, comprising six baby boys and six baby girls. HTA director Dr Shamsul Anuar Kamarudin said a birth on National Day is not only a special date, but it also carries a deeper meaning as a symbol of life, hope and the nation’s future.

items.title: Nine students injured after school bus carrying 36 crashes in Sabah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Nine students from Sekolah Menengah (SM) Sains Sabah suffered minor injuries after a bus carrying 35 students and a teacher was involved in an accident on the Kota Belud-Kundasang road in Sabah this morning. Kota Belud Fire and Rescue Station chief Elge Bakuk said firefighters were dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call. “All the victims were later taken to Kota Belud Hospital for further treatment using ambulances from the Health Ministry in Tuaran and Kota Belud, as well as an ambulance from the Malaysian Civil Defence Force,” he said.

items.title: Customs sniffer dogs Goku and Cafrey join military K9s marching at Putrajaya National Day
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — While their daily routine involves tracking drugs at national entry points or performing military guard duty, K9 dogs Goku and Troy share a common mission today, namely marching alongside 33 other dogs at the National Day parade in Dataran Putrajaya. Johnson Pedro said that initial training for the parade involved walking the dogs individually before pairing them with compatible dogs to march side by side. “Military dogs are highly trained.

items.title: Suspect arrested after teen shot when hunting companion mistakes him for animal in Sarawak
items.summary: MIRI, Aug 31 — The shooting case involving a 17-year-old teenager in Long Lidong, Lawas, has been resolved with the arrest of a suspect on August 25, said Lawas district police chief DSP Liong Tindan. Liong said following the arrest of the suspect, the police also recovered a homemade firearm, locally known as a ‘ bakakuk ’, believed to have been used in the incident. “The police are continuing investigations, including tracing witnesses and gathering other information related to the case.

items.title: Kuskop to expedite disbursement of PM’s additional RM1b microcredit pledge, says minister
items.summary: SERDANG, Aug 31 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives (Kuskop) will expedite the disbursement of an additional RM1 billion in microcredit funds to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement yesterday. Minister Steven Sim said the increase in allocation brings this year’s total microcredit funding to RM6 billion, up from RM5 billion. Yesterday, Anwar, who is also finance minister, announced the additional RM1 billion in micro financing facilities and said the government had agreed to raise the e-invoice exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million annually.

items.title: Election Commission to reveal proposed new, renamed Sarawak state seats on Sept 1
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 31 — The names and locations of Sarawak’s 17 proposed new State Legislative Assembly (DUN) constituencies will finally be publicly unveiled by the Election Commission (EC) tomorrow (September 1). The announcement is eagerly anticipated as it will provide greater clarity on the proposed expansion of the Sarawak Legislative Assembly from 82 to 99 seats, following the redelineation exercise undertaken by the EC. Apart from the new seats, the EC has proposed renaming several existing seats.

items.title: Penang council seizes licensed dog after viral video shows attack on stray in Tanjung Bungah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Penang authorities have seized a licensed dog after a viral video showed it repeatedly attacking a smaller stray in Tanjung Bungah, with the incident now under investigation under the Animal Welfare Act 2015. According to The Star , the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) said it seized the dog today after receiving a complaint through its official WhatsApp channel yesterday over the incident at Pearl Hill. MBPP said checks found that the dog had a valid licence and was registered as a mixed breed.

items.title: ‘Ultraman’ detained near main stage ahead of Sultan Nazrin’s arrival at Perak National Day celebration, says state police chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — A man dressed as Ultraman was detained near the main stage at Perak’s National Day celebrations today after police said his behaviour appeared suspicious in an area where Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah and other members of the Perak royal family were due to be seated. According to Berita Harian , Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the local man, who is in his 40s, was detained at about 5am after he was seen entering and lingering near the main stage area. Also present were Raja Muda Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja Di Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Idris Shah, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and members of the state executive council.

items.title: Malaysia Day 2026: Final prep meeting set for Sept 5 ahead of Kuching celebration, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — A meeting to review the final preparations for the 2026 Malaysia Day celebration in Kuching, Sarawak, will be held on September 5, ahead of the main event at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) on September 16. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the official celebration would take place on the night of September 16, with various side events lined up around BCCK and Plaza Merdeka to enliven the Malaysia Day festivities. Fahmi, who is also chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) main committee, said he was confident that Malaysians from across the country would attend the event, which would feature an exhibition tracing the history of Malaysia’s formation.

items.title: ‘Habis madu, sepah dibuang’: Anthony Loke posts Malay proverb after Ong Kian Ming quits DAP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today posted a Malay proverb on Facebook shortly after former Bangi MP Ong Kian Ming announced his resignation from the party after 14 years. “ Habis madu, sepah dibuang ,” Loke wrote in the brief post. Ong announced earlier today that his resignation from DAP would take effect today, bringing to an end his membership of the party since 2012.

items.title: Voice behind National Day air show, Major Dinnesh brings fighter jet manoeuvres alive
items.summary: The role of air show commentator, says Dinnesh, a 34-year-old Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officer, goes far beyond reading a script into a microphone. “That was where my career as an air show commentator with the RMAF began,” said the officer, who now serves in the RMAF Air Defence Control Division, in an interview with Bernama. For the 2026 National Day parade and march-past, Dinnesh took on the role of air commentator alongside Major Neny Suhaida Ab Suki and Captain Muhammad Iqbal Nasrudin.

items.title: Roar of fighter jets dominates Putrajaya skies as RMAF stages National Day air show
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — The roar of fighter jets reverberated across the skies over Putrajaya today as the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) staged a thrilling air display, one of the highlights of the 69th National Day celebration. Royal Malaysian Air Force chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris once again took to the cockpit of a Sukhoi Su-30MKM to lead the display, marking the second consecutive year he has personally led the National Day air show. Four Su-30MKMs, four F/A-18D Hornets and three BAE Hawk 208 fighter jets thundered across the skies, showcasing the nation’s air capabilities and operational readiness.

items.title: Malaysia’s King and Queen mark 69th National Day, send greetings to all citizens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Malaysia’s King and Queen, Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, extended 69th National Day greetings to all Malaysians. The royal message was conveyed through a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook page today. Earlier, Their Majesties arrived at the National Day celebration in Putrajaya at 8am and were received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr. Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, as well as Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who also serves as chairman of the National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 Main Committee.

items.title: Sarawak to carry out cloud seeding Sept 3 to 5 as haze worsens, four water plants shut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Sarawak will carry out cloud seeding from September 3 to 5 as authorities grapple with worsening haze and critically low reservoir levels that have already forced four water treatment plants to stop operating. According to Harian Metro , Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) expected conditions to be suitable for the operation during the three-day window. Uggah, who chairs the committee, said the Rural Water Supply Department had reported that four water treatment plants had been forced to suspend operations because reservoir levels had fallen too low.

items.title: Sarawak says no emergency unless API breaches 500, Serian readings remain hazardous
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 31 — A state of emergency will only be declared if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 500 or above under the National Haze Action Plan, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas. The Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman clarified that there is currently no necessity to declare a state of emergency yet. Both readings remain within the hazardous level.

items.title: National Day reflections: Zahid stresses TVET jobs, Fadillah calls for harmony and shared future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The meaning of independence must be reflected in people’s lives by ensuring they have access to skills, better employment opportunities and are not left behind in the nation’s development, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Ahmad Zahid said the struggle today was no longer about achieving independence, but ensuring that its true meaning remained alive in the lives of the people. He said independence should also create opportunities for small entrepreneurs to grow and enable every family to improve their lives.

items.title: ‘Not today’: Gobind keeps politics off the table on National Day as questions turn to Ong Kian Ming’s DAP resignation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo today declined to comment on former Bangi MP Ong Kian Ming’s resignation from the party, saying National Day was not the time for politics. According to the New Straits Times , Gobind said he had yet to read Ong’s statement and deferred any response to another time. No politics today.

items.title: ‘Great show!’ Anwar thanks Malaysians, mingles with crowds at National Day parade
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim praised and expressed his appreciation to everyone involved, as well as members of the public who attended the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya here today. “Great, great show! One member of the crowd even thanked the Prime Minister for restoring the monthly basic eligibility quota under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme from 200 litres to 300 litres, which he announced during the National Day Prime Minister’s Address yesterday.
